NEW SPEED RECORD!! Managed to get it going 55 mph for the first time.

Taught my prepping partner how to drive it. It was the first time he'd been in it since I bought it and he said that the difference in how it ran and drove between now and then is like night and day. Amazing when a few bits of regular maintenance will do for a vehicle. All told, not including tires, I've dropped maybe $1200 in mechanic cost on the truck and that was only because for most of that I don't have tools capable of working on something that heavy duty. (First goal was to get it completely up to snuff THEN get the tools - better to have the truck running 100% and not have the tools than to have the tools and need a truck at 100% when it isn't.).

In any case, the driving lesson went pretty well. There were many missed gears and lots of confusion on how to start it (he's a slow learner). But after about 30 minutes, he was comfortable enough with it to take it around the mall instead of just weaving through the parking lot.

Still on the list: Air filter change just because, exhaust, minor air leak behind the console (likely at the air gauge), replacing the windshield glass (lots of scratches and air bubbles, difficult to see through in direct sunlight), paint job, double check to see if the fuel density compensator has been bypassed (and remove the bypass if it has). I have no delusions about how expensive that is going to be but then again, new drop-in campers for pickups can go as high as $100K so building it myself will be infinity cheaper.
